content: Before starting darunavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. If you are pregnant, notify your doctor before using this medication, as treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Be aware that this medication can pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is essential to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share this with your doctor and pharmacist. Darunavir can slow the elimination of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. Similarly, other medications can influence how darunavir is removed from your body, which may impact its effectiveness. Examples of such medications include apalutamide, garlic supplements, certain rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifapentine), and others. Additionally, darunavir may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods like pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests (e.g., liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol, blood sugar) are necessary. If you miss a dose of darunavir taken twice daily, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than six hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. For once-daily dosing, take the missed dose as soon as you remember, unless it is less than 12 hours before the next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid form in its original container and avoid refrigerating or freezing it. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Darunavir is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. Darunavir belongs to a class of drugs called protease inhibitors and must be taken with certain other medications (e.g., cobicistat, ritonavir) to boost its levels in the body. It is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications as prescribed and use effective barrier methods (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms/dental dams) during sexual activity. Avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or body fluids. Take this medication by mouth with food as directed by your doctor. Darunavir must be taken at the same time as certain other medications, usually once or twice daily. The dosage is based on your age, lab tests, medical condition, and response to treatment. For optimal results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less than prescribed or stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s guidance. Common side effects of darunavir include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and headache. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune system may cause symptoms at any time, even months after starting HIV treatment. Rarely, darunavir may increase blood sugar levels, potentially causing or worsening diabetes. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar regularly and share the results with your doctor. In rare cases, darunavir may cause serious, potentially fatal liver problems. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare, but darunavir can commonly cause a rash that is usually not severe. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
